purpose: Record actual CSD lane trials so the lane system is tested, not only described.

trials.objective: Import Claude-side lane know-how and make one CSD lane trial visible.
claude_knowhow: Dashboard acts as a control plane: purpose, state, progress, quality, and policy are visible in one place.
Use five-line/small-ticket instructions: purpose, input, output, verification, report shape.
Acceptance is not just generated output; use apply check, real artifact check, and occasional break-detection.
Do not stack work into the same lane; keep one bounded ticket per run.
Keep generated dashboards reproducible and avoid hand-editing generated output.

trials.do: Add this trial ledger and show it on CSD.

trials.act: Record the trial in HUB/progress and set the next lane ticket.
trials.next_ticket: Use Static Tool Lane to clean visible CSD mojibake labels in the dashboard generator.

trials.objective: Create sample content from GO/HOSHI shared web design know-how and show it on CSD.
claude_knowhow: HTML First: deliver as a single readable HTML file.
Easy Japanese: short sentences, clear verbs, and concrete action labels.
Gentle slope: useful without settings, with optional controls only when needed.
Export path: every small tool should offer JSON or Markdown output.
Real artifact check: generated output is not complete until the actual page is opened and reviewed.
trials.plan: Use a compact read of shared upper_design references and create one CODEX-owned sample.
trials.check: Run syntax, JSON, dashboard, and public-copy visibility checks.
trials.act: Show Web Designer Sample Lane and sample artifact on CSD.
trials.next_ticket: Run browser visual check for CSD Web Designer Sample.

trials.objective: Create a stronger web-design showcase content artifact and make it visible through CSD.
claude_knowhow: Lane output should become a usable artifact, not only a status note.
Visual control planes should make purpose, state, check, and next action visible quickly.
High-quality repeated output depends on a compact ticket, fixed acceptance, and reusable export shape.
Use actual visual material when judging web-design quality.
Keep the artifact portable so another AI or reviewer can continue from a small export.

trials.next_ticket: Run browser visual checks for CSD Designer Showcase and clean CSD mojibake labels.

trials.objective: Create an actual content lane from the theme: make people more interested in cats.
claude_knowhow: A lane is not an explanation; it includes the artifact, ledger update, QC, and dashboard listing.
Single HTML, offline-friendly content and export routes are preferred for cloud/GO-style lanes.
Reuse asset/design/response patterns so future lanes cost less and keep quality.
CG is the main listing surface; CSD remains the detailed check surface.
Small interaction should feel like response, not just decoration.

trials.act: Register Cat Affinity Lane in CG/CSD ledgers and leave the next response-pattern ticket.
trials.next_ticket: Add optional purr sound using shared procedural sound recipe and a too-much-touch response state.

trials.objective: Confirm CG freshness and create one publishable content artifact for 2026-07-31.
claude_knowhow: Keep the task bounded to one objective and one visible artifact.
CG should show the newest usable result first.
Every small app needs an export path so handoff does not require rereading context.
CSD/status ledgers should agree with the published entry.
Single HTML keeps mobile publication cheap and easy to inspect.

trials.objective: Increase CG listed content with one more small usable artifact.
claude_knowhow: A listed content item should be useful on first open.
Small tools need local save and export paths.
Keep controls familiar: preset buttons, start, pause, reset, complete.
Make the latest content visible on CG and the ledger visible on CSD.
Do not use GPU or local LLM for a simple static content lane.

trials.objective: Visualize Codex eco-lane implementation on CG.
claude_knowhow: Claude/Codex should act as command tower for small tickets, acceptance, and checks.
Implementation should reuse narrow single-HTML patterns.
Token saving is strongest when the lane itself is visible and reusable.
CG is the public entry; CSD is the detailed control plane.
Each lane should leave a compact next ticket instead of a long retrospective.

trials.next_ticket: Use Eco Lane Map before creating the next CG-listed content item.

trials.objective: Create a mobile-first compressor for external AI briefs.
claude_knowhow: Smartphone-first input should favor choices over long typing.
Codex should prepare compact briefs before handing work to external AI or Web.
The prompt should include purpose, target, output format, tone, checks, and constraints.
Copy plus JSON/Markdown export keeps the handoff cheap.
The tool should work as a single HTML file with no external service.

trials.act: Register External AI Brief Compressor in CG/CSD ledgers as the first practical tool for the external AI lane.
trials.next_ticket: Use this compressor to create the next CG content brief before implementation.

trials.objective: Expand the brief compressor into a multi-genre lane selector with Codex task-list output.
claude_knowhow: Smartphone operation benefits from preset lanes and short text fields.
Creative work needs many patterns: MV, music, lyrics, image, illustration, game, app, article, and research.
A compressor should decide whether the output goes to chat copy, external AI/Web, or a Codex task list.
Complex media such as MV should expose component lanes for music, lyrics, image, and video structure.
Local task-list storage reduces repeated prompt writing.

trials.objective: Turn the compressor into a GO-ready task control panel.
claude_knowhow: A compressed brief should remove ambiguity before Codex starts work.
The user needs to see whether a task is only set or explicitly approved with GO.
Rough token estimates are useful as planning hints but must not pretend to be exact.
Genre lanes should work for apps, music, images, videos, MV, games, articles, and research using the same control model.
A mobile-first control panel should turn choices into target files, acceptance, checks, and handoff exports.

trials.act: Use the compressor as the default pre-execution gate for future CG content creation.
trials.next_ticket: Use this GO-ready compressor to create the next CG-listed artifact from a selected task.

trials.objective: Create and test one complete CODEX eco-lane by building a serious smartphone puzzle game from command-tower brief to CG/CSD registration.
claude_knowhow: A serious lane should finish with a usable artifact, not only a planning note.
External AI work should be framed as compact briefs, level ideas, review points, and bounded improvements.
Codex should integrate the result into single HTML, verify behavior, export handoff material, and register ledgers.
Smartphone-first games need tap controls, stable board dimensions, local progress, and no setup.
The next ticket should be a level-pack or review loop, not a broad ecosystem reread.

trials.objective: Create a completely different serious puzzle game app through the same CODEX eco-lane pattern while saving tokens.
claude_knowhow: Do not reuse the same core mechanic when the request asks for a different app.
For token saving, keep external AI scope to level packs, hint text, and bounded review, while Codex owns integration and verification.
A serious puzzle needs deterministic validation, not only visual play.
Smartphone-first number games need large tap targets, fixed board dimensions, Undo, Hint, and local records.
A completed eco-lane should register the artifact in CG/CSD and leave the next level-pack ticket.

Falling games need deterministic collision, line clearing, input, pause/reset, and result export before visual polish is considered done.
Smartphone-first play needs large touch controls and stable canvas framing.
The next ticket should be a mission pack or balance pass, not a broad redesign.
